title: The Lights of Geoncheonggung
synopsis: The first electric lamps of Korea go dark for an hour.
In the dark, two strangers walk through the Queen's court.
goal: Find out what the strangers were doing in the dark, and why the Queen is in danger.

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene): Lady Han's water-drop note lies under the coal scoop; the lamp machine opens the three choice pictures once it is read.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheet of lamp_house.webp (picture.measuredOn): the scoop and the note lower left, the window with the pavilion, the engine with its wheel and belt, the coal heap, the open door, the wires along the top; no two areas overlap.

The three choice pictures differ by what the note says (the fire, the coal, the leather belt on the big wheel), never by colour alone. The note is drawn as a blank paper with a small blue water-drop mark: no writing in any picture.
Puzzle kind chosen by hand: the season spread assigns Case 05 a look round with a picture choice (PART 10 brief); the note is read in the place, then the part is matched by its words.

learning.objective: 궁녀 한씨의 쪽지에서 did not touch 문장(불, 석탄)을 읽어 지우고, 낯선 이가 벗겨 낸 것(큰 바퀴의 가죽 띠)을 그림에서 고른다.
expressions: He did not touch the fire.
He took off the long leather belt.

play.title: The Lamp House
story: South of the pond stands the lamp house.
Its machine makes the light for the King's and the Queen's halls.
Last night it stopped for an hour. Who stopped it? Look for marks.
play.letterIntro: Under the coal scoop, a note in the King's letters, with a small water drop:
play.letter:
Detective,
Last night the lamps did not go out on their own.
A stranger came into the lamp house.
He did not touch the fire. He did not touch the coal.
He took off the long leather belt that turns the big wheel.
I put it back at dawn. His muddy hand is still on it.
— Han
play.question: What did the stranger touch? Tap one picture.
hints: Find the note under the coal scoop first. Then look at the machine.
Two things in the note are things he did NOT touch.
play.successMessage: A muddy hand mark on the belt!
transition: The lamps often blink on and off. Everyone thought it was that again.
But this dark was made on purpose.
The note is signed Han. You go to find her.

clue.title: The Dark Was Made
clue.note: The lamps did not fail. A stranger took the belt off the big wheel on purpose.

So the strangers hid in a dark that seemed normal.

discovery.title: THE DARK WAS MADE
discovery.detail: Someone took the belt off on purpose. The strangers needed the dark.

notes: Letter: Lady Han's account of the night, in before/after words. 8:00 and 9:00 are fixed; the guards at the main gate are not part of it (another gate, every night).
Every card is made up (fiction): the night and the strangers are the case's own.

clueInputs.note: The dark was made: the belt was taken off.
Duri's water-drop note from the rebuilt palace: the same small water drop.

learning.objective: 한씨의 진술에서 after, first, before 표현을 읽고 그날 밤 일을 시간 순서로 놓는다.
expressions: They left before the lamp man came back.

play.title: One Hour in the Dark
story: Lady Han meets you in the Queen's court.
She was awake last night. She saw where the strangers went.
"Put my words in order," she says. "Then you will see."
play.letter:
The lamp man lit the lamps at 8:00.
The lamps went dark after the strangers came into the lamp house.
In the dark, the men went to the east gate of the court first.
After the gate, they stood by the Queen's hall and counted.
They left before the lamp man came back.
The lamp man came back at 9:00.
The guards at the main gate saw nothing. They are far away.
play.question: Put the night in order, from 8:00 to 9:00.
hints: Look for the words first, after and before in Lady Han's account.
The main gate is far away. Is it part of that night?
play.successMessage: The strangers walked straight to the Queen's hall!
transition: From the east gate to the Queen's hall, in one hour of dark.
She opens her sewing box. Inside is a long rope with knots.
play.orderFeedback: Read Lady Han's words again. Where did the men go first?

lines.text: I serve the Queen. I sleep near her rooms.
Last night I heard steps in the dark.
Then tell me everything, in order.

clueInputs.note: The strangers counted between the east gate and the Queen's hall.

learning.objective: 매듭 규칙(A big knot is ten steps. A small knot is one step.)을 읽고 매듭 수를 걸음 수로 바꿔 입력한다.
expressions: A big knot is ten steps.
three big knots, then seven small knots

play.title: The Knotted Rope
story: Lady Han found the rope by the Queen's hall at dawn.
One stranger dropped it as the lamps came back.
It is a measuring rope. Its knots count steps.
play.letterIntro: Lady Han shows you the rope and says:
play.letter:
Builders measure with ropes like this.
A big knot is ten steps. A small knot is one step.
The rope starts at the east gate.
It ends at the Queen's door.
On it are three big knots, then seven small knots.
play.question: How many steps is it from the east gate to the Queen's door?
hints: Read what one big knot means, and what one small knot means.
Count the big knots in tens. Then add the small knots.
play.successMessage: Thirty-seven steps, from the east gate to the Queen's door!
transition: "Last night they dropped a board too. I hid it before anyone saw."
"It has a number on it. The King must see it now."

feedback.10: That counts every knot as one step. A big knot is ten steps.
feedback.30: You counted the big knots. Now add the small ones.
feedback.73: The big knots are tens, not ones. Read Lady Han's rule again.

play.orderFeedback: The right numbers, in the wrong order. Big knots are the tens.

clue.title: Thirty-Seven Steps
clue.note: The rope measures 37 steps from the east gate to the Queen's door.

evidence.name: The Knotted Rope
evidence.description: A stranger's measuring rope: 37 steps from the east gate to the Queen's door.

discovery.title: THEY MEASURED THE WAY
discovery.detail: Nobody measures a path for no reason. What were they making?

notes: The answer is the case's key fact (h4): in 1895 the Queen worked with Russia to hold back Japan's power in Korea. Russia is the country she worked with, not the one she held back.
The Queen's and the King's words are made up (dossier fiction); Lady Han's last line retells h4 only.
Puzzle kind chosen by hand: the season spread assigns Case 05 a word entry final; the answer is one word read and told apart in Lady Han's sentence.

clueInputs.note: The dark was made on purpose.
The strangers walked to the Queen's hall.
37 steps to the Queen's door: the same number as on the board.

learning.objective: worked with Russia to hold back Japan's power 문장을 읽고, 왕비가 함께한 나라와 막으려 한 나라를 구별해 쓴다.

play.title: The Board with No Names
story: Lady Han brings the strangers' board to the King's hall.
On it are lines for halls and doors, and a path from the east gate.
By one door, 37 is written on the board. It is a map of the Queen's rooms.
The Queen looks at it in silence. "Someone is afraid of me," she says.
play.letterIntro: Your notes, and Lady Han's words to the King:
play.letter:
The dark was made on purpose.
The strangers walked from the east gate to the Queen's hall.
The rope and the map both say 37 steps to the Queen's door.
Lady Han says: "Japan's power in Korea is growing.
The Queen works with Russia to hold back Japan's power.
Some men want her out of the way."
play.question: Whose power is the Queen trying to hold back?
hints: Read Lady Han's words. Two countries are named.
One country works WITH the Queen. Which one does she hold back?
play.successMessage: The Queen holds back Japan's power. That is why she is watched.
transition: The King folds the map slowly.
Every path of this palace has been counted in steps.
Lady Han puts her note in a small wooden box.

feedback.RUSSIA: The Queen works WITH Russia. Read Lady Han's words again.
feedback.CHINA: China is not in Lady Han's words. Which two countries does she name?
feedback.KOREA: The Queen is Korea's Queen. Whose power is growing in Korea?

evidence.name: The Strangers' Map
evidence.description: A map of the Queen's rooms, drawn in the dark by strangers. Lady Han found it first. The palace is watched.

ending.text: Thank you, Detective. I will keep this map.

objectives: Find out why the lamps went dark.
Count the steps on the rope.
Tell the King why the Queen is watched.
intro: Autumn, 1895. You are a guest at Geoncheonggung, inside Gyeongbokgung.
Here the King lives in Jangandang, and the Queen in Gonnyeonhap.
In 1887, the first electric lamps in Korea were lit here.
They often blink on and off. People call them the good-for-nothing lights.
Last night they went dark for an hour.
And two strangers were seen in the Queen's court.
play.caseSummary: Strangers made the lamps go dark and measured the way to the Queen's door. Court Lady Han found their map first. In 1895 the Queen worked with Russia to hold back Japan's power. On 8 October 1895, men sent by Japan's minister attacked the palace, and the Queen was killed.

notes: Season 5 Case 05 (PART 10, 2026-11-06). Set weeks before the Eulmi incident; the attack is told once, plainly, in the final's ending and the reveal, never shown.

The Queen is never drawn with a detailed face: no reliable photograph of her is known, and her portrait is seen from behind (manifest). She, the King and Lady Han speak made-up words (dossier fiction).
Case 06 recalls s5_ep05_e4 (the strangers' map: the palace is watched).
